subject: Creativity
title: Absurdist Comedy: When Logic Is the Joke
description: A quick, practical guide to Absurdist Comedy: When Logic Is the Joke.

hook.text: Monty Python: 'Nobody expects the Spanish Inquisition!' Then cardinals burst in with soft cushions as torture devices.

buildup.text: Absurdist comedy rejects logic entirely. It builds a world where expectations no longer apply.

discovery.text: It emerged after World War II — when Beckett, Ionesco, and Camus showed that reality was already absurd.

twist.text: Adult Swim, Tim & Eric, and Eric Andre carry the torch — comedy so bizarre it questions what comedy even is.

climax.text: Absurdist humor tests the brain's pattern-recognition limits.

punchline.text: In absurdist comedy, the joke isn't what happens.

quiz.question: What philosophical movement influenced absurdist comedy?
options: Post-WWII existentialism and the philosophy of Camus and Beckett
